solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so the letters of the preceding words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes where in the sky the planet Mars was photographed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' tells you to rearrange LOCATION and MARS together; 'with' simply joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things relating to the stars and heavens, a straight synonym pair.

clue.text: A bishop taking hold shows authority

indicators.note: a bishop taking something holds it within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the formal style of a bishop
to bite is to grip or hold, as a screw or anchor bites

explanation.surface: A churchman who grabs hold of something displays his power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' signals the container; Right Reverend is the formal style of a bishop, and 'shows' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person with power to settle disputes, someone acting as an authority.

parts.note: to rove is to travel or wander about

explanation.surface: A time-travel adventure turns up buried treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuable things found concealed, as in treasure trove.

indicators.note: the retainer comes after, following, the old boy in the answer

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a retainer is a household servant

explanation.surface: A loyal family servant walks behind an elderly gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' signals the order; an old boy in Britain is a former pupil of a particular school.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant can mean diligent in keeping rules or customs, so dutiful in observance.

parts.note: pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: A convict escapes from an ancient jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break out' is used as in 'break out the champagne'; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To break out a bottle or supplies is to open it up for use, an idiomatic equivalent.

definitions.meaning: to split is slang for informing on someone, so 'split's' reads as has split, has grassed
to fill someone in is to tell them the facts, to bring them up to date

explanation.definitionFit: Informed means both grassed on someone to the authorities and told someone the news.

clue.text: A new terrorist leader in charge of caper

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fresh terror chief takes control of a criminal escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or absurd prank, much the same as a caper.

clue.text: Smart, if I cease revealing cunning

indicators.note: the words reveal, uncover, a run of letters that lies inside them

explanation.surface: A smart person stops being clever and shows their true wiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing' shows the answer inside sm-ART IF I CE-ase.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever trickery or craft, the same as cunning used as a noun.

clue.text: With men transformed, she concocted trap

indicators.note: transformed means changed, so the letters of men are rearranged
concocted means cooked up, so the letters of she are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman devises a snare to catch the men she has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' turns MEN into ENM and 'concocted' turns SHE into ESH; 'With' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to catch as in a net, so to entangle or trap.

clue.text: Where volume may be turned up?

definitions.text: Where volume may be turned up?

parts.words: Where volume may be turned up?
parts.note: reads like sound volume being increased, but a volume is a book that may be found, turned up, on a shelf

explanation.definitionFit: A book, or volume, is stored and so can be located on a shelf made for books.

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to turn is to fashion or shape, as on a lathe
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian city is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I (Italy, from its car registration code) inside TURN; 'of' is a link and 'in fashion' is not a phrase here.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: People in authority holding alternative view

indicators.note: the people in authority hold, contain, the alternative

parts.note: they, as in 'why don't they do something', means the powers that be
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Officials take a different line on an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the container; the definers are the vague 'they' of everyday complaint, the powers that be.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is an opinion or idea held about something, a view.

indicators.note: the worth catches, holds within it, the performance

parts.note: price means worth or value
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A valuable dress rehearsal is caught on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' signals the container; 'Worth' opens the clue as if it were an adjective but it is a noun, value.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is a rehearsal, a run-through before the real thing.

clue.text: Letting concrete set around middle of lintel

indicators.note: the concrete is set around, enclosing, the other piece

parts.note: real means concrete, actual

indicators.note: the middle letters of a word with an even count are its central pair

explanation.surface: Builders let concrete set round the centre of a doorway lintel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central pair of the six-letter lintel and 'set around' signals the container; 'Letting' is a noun, a property let out.
explanation.definitionFit: A letting is a property let to tenants, which is a rental.

parts.note: reads like a near result in a match, but a score is twenty and this number is just one short of it

explanation.definitionFit: Nineteen is one fewer than twenty, the number called a score.

indicators.note: the carp goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: a carp is a fish
ever means always

explanation.surface: A grumbler who always complains gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' reads as a verb, complain, but it is the fish; 'about' signals the container and 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means frenzied and restless, so agitated or excited.

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to execute is to kill

explanation.surface: The state carries out an execution by lethal injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injection' signals the container; 'Government' means the executive branch, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The executive is the branch of government that carries out the laws.

indicators.note: the fraud holds, contains, the press

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a fraud
the media means the press

explanation.surface: A conman carries a fake press pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like the press card, but it is the definition, an amusing person; 'holding' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a witty or eccentric person, someone who makes others laugh.

clue.text: Con isn't worried receiving a punishment

indicators.note: the jumbled letters receive, take in, the A
worried in the sense of pulled about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An anxious convict learns his penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the seven letters of the first two words into SNCTION, and 'receiving' puts A inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is a penalty imposed for breaking a rule, a punishment.

definitions.meaning: to train someone is to teach or drill them
a set is a group sharing outlook

explanation.definitionFit: School is a verb meaning to educate and a noun for a group of like-minded people.

definitions.meaning: a break from work, such as a parliamentary holiday
a hollow or alcove set back in a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break from business and also an indentation or niche.

definitions.meaning: to arrest is to halt or stop something temporarily
to hang something is to dangle it from above

explanation.definitionFit: Suspend means both to halt for a time and to hang from a support.

clue.text: Pension owner from the Loire, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A French guesthouse keeper hails from the Loire valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' is the French word for a boarding house; 'perhaps' rearranges THE LOIRE and 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a pension, a small guesthouse, keeps a hotel.

indicators.note: of here means taken from, a run of letters drawn from within the words

explanation.surface: Pages of a novel written in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals that the answer lies inside nove-L IN EN-glish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedclothes such as sheets and pillowcases are collectively called household linen.

clue.text: Flipping drink after drink, creating disturbance

indicators.note: the flipped drink comes after the second drink in the answer

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Downing drink after drink leads to a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' turns the verb meaning drink into PUS, and 'after' sets that behind the spirit; 'creating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or uproar, a disturbance.

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a worker ant is the commonest crossword worker

explanation.surface: A quiet labourer on a production line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' is a noun here, a factory; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial site, a factory or works.

indicators.note: hearing signals that a word heard sounds like the answer

parts.note: 'I will' shortened is the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: A man promises, briefly, that he will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' leads to disguise its capital: the Isle of Man is an island between Britain and Ireland; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island, so Man is one such island.

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: A poem is recited for an audience at a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: ODEON is a British cinema chain, and the word means a building for performances.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon was originally a Greek building for musical performance, hence a theatre.

clue.text: Egg on toast's starter — is eating out, outside

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go outside, around, the single letter
out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Egg on toast is the first thing someone orders when eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the two words into INSIGATE, 'starter' takes the opening letter of toast, and 'outside' wraps the jumble around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to urge or provoke it, to egg it on.

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected turn, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude teenager is, unexpectedly, not bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges TEEN ISNT RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninterested feels no curiosity or concern, the state of being bored.
